name: Glass as an identity
art: The folded mark is original procedural geometry. Its optical backing plane and typography are composed inside the renderer and are actually sampled through the glass. This is a known scene, not arbitrary DOM refraction.

properties.label: Hero mark beside scale proof
properties.text: Place a large translucent sculptural mark on the right of a pale green editorial page. Pair a simple left headline with progressively sized flat versions of the same mark so the relationship between identity and material is explicit.

properties.label: Shared folded mark silhouette
properties.text: Use one folded silhouette for both the large volume and crisp flat vector marks, retaining its meaningful cutouts and direction at small sizes.

properties.label: Polished refracting identity glass
properties.text: Use a clear polished volume with a restrained cool cast, tight bevels, alternating dark and bright edge intervals and softly grounded depth. Place a typographic plane genuinely behind it so refraction is visible.

properties.label: Sage-white and deep green
properties.text: Use a sage-white ground and deep green type, leaving the glass clear with only a restrained cool cast.

properties.label: Quiet thickness reveal
properties.text: A very quiet rotation or pointer reaction may reveal thickness. Use an actual modeled mark for a changing viewpoint and a matching composed poster fallback; keep small marks as crisp vectors.

properties.label: Landmark refraction check
properties.text: Inspect an actual landmark through the volume and its unchanged portion outside it, both at rest and under a changing view.

properties.label: Coherent clear optical finish
properties.text: Look for coherent thickness and reflections with a readable clear center. A mint fill or transmission setting alone does not prove the intended optical finish.
